plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of what other bidders do, since you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) if you win. Overbidding risks winning and paying more than the item is worth; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since other bidders are rational and will also bid truthfully, I should bid my true value of $21 to ensure optimal outcomes in expectation.

In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because your payment only depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid (as long as you win), so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable trades. Since this holds true irrespective of what others do, I will bid exactly my value of $22.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy - it doesn't matter what others bid or think about my strategy. If I bid above my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me. If I bid below, I risk losing an item I'd profit from. Therefore, regardless of the other bidders' rationality or beliefs, my optimal action is to bid exactly my true value of $13.
